title: Big Stars Left Out: England's World Cup Squad Surprises!
summary: Imagine training your whole life for the World Cup, and then finding out you didn't make the team. That's what happened to some of England's biggest soccer stars! Coach Thomas Tuchel announced his 26-player squad, and Phil Foden, Cole Palmer, and Trent Alexander-Arnold are not on the list. Harry Maguire, a defender for Manchester United, was also left out. He posted on Instagram that he was 'shocked and gutted.' His mom even said she was 'disgusted' by the decision. But there are some happy surprises too. Ollie Watkins made it after helping his team win the Europa League. Ivan Toney, who scored 32 goals in 32 games in Saudi Arabia, is also going. Djed Spence got picked even though he broke his jaw recently—he might wear a protective mask! The World Cup is this summer, and everyone will be watching to see if Tuchel's choices lead England to victory.
why_it_matters: This shows that in sports, even the most talented players can be left out if a coach has a different plan, teaching us that hard work and current form matter more than reputation.

background_read: The World Cup is soccer's biggest tournament, held every four years. England won it once, in 1966, and fans have waited almost 60 years for another title.

Coach Thomas Tuchel, a German who previously managed clubs like Chelsea and Bayern Munich, surprised many by dropping famous players like Phil Foden (a star for Manchester City) and Harry Maguire (a defender for Manchester United).
Article_Structure: WHO: England's national soccer team coach Thomas Tuchel and players like Phil Foden, Harry Maguire, Ollie Watkins, and Djed Spence.
WHAT: Tuchel announced a 26-player World Cup squad, leaving out some big stars and including surprise picks.
WHERE: England (the squad announcement for the tournament).
WHY: Tuchel made his choices to build the best team for the World Cup, even if it meant upsetting famous players.

perspectives.description: Surprise picks like Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney get a chance to shine on the world stage, showing that good club performances can earn a spot.
Leaving out stars like Foden and Palmer could weaken the team, and fans and families are upset because they feel these players deserved to go.
Coaches have to make tough decisions to find the right balance of players, and different styles of play mean some famous names won't fit the plan.
